name: hcapp_deletePasskey
description: Removes one passkey from the calling hasher's account (E9.F7.S18) by clearing the four credential columns (PasskeyCredentialId, PasskeyPublicKey, PasskeyCounter, PasskeyTransports) on that HC.Device row. The DEVICE ROW SURVIVES: it still holds the device secret that signs this hasher's API calls, so deleting the passkey does not sign the browser out — it only removes one-tap sign-in. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 120, standard token — the only reachable target is the caller's own credential, so a compound token would add a failure mode without removing a risk). Authorization: @userId comes from the token and the UPDATE is scoped to UserId = @userId, so a forged @targetDeviceId belonging to someone else matches no row and is reported as 'not found' (1951), revealing nothing. Idempotent in effect: a passkey already gone is also 'not found'. A revoked passkey is then refused at sign-in by publicWeb_getPasskey finding no row. On success the reply carries the hasher's REMAINING passkeys in the shape of hcapp_listPasskeys so the screen can repaint from the reply.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device making the call. Default NULL. Also used to flag IsThisDevice in the remaining-passkeys rowset and recorded in the LOG.GeneralLog audit line ('by=').

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token (standard, device secret). Default NULL.

parameters.name: targetDeviceId
parameters.description: The HC.Device row whose passkey is removed. Default NULL → 1950 'Missing fields'. Must belong to the caller, be live (removed = 0) and hold a PasskeyCredentialId → else 1951 'Not found'.

rowsets.description: Auth failure (ValidateAppAuth: 1220/1320 + signed-out 1220 errorType 7) returns the error detail ALONE — no envelope row before it.

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: On a refusal after auth: { success = 0, errorCode, errorType } then the detail at index 1. 1950 missing targetDeviceId (errorType 2); 1951 passkey not found / not yours / already gone (3); 1952 unhandled (5) — on that path the envelope is { success = 0, errorMessage = ERROR_MESSAGE() } instead.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: 1950 / 1951. (Absent on the CATCH path, which emits errorMessage.)

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: On success: the standard success envelope.

rowsets.name: Passkeys
rowsets.description: On success: the hasher's REMAINING passkey-bearing live devices, newest sign-in first — identical in shape to hcapp_listPasskeys rowset 1. May be empty.

columns.name: Label
columns.description: 'Safari on iPhone', 'Harrier Central on iPhone' — from Device.OperatingSystem / IsMobile and HC6.DevicePlatformName(DeviceData).

columns.name: IsThisDevice
columns.description: 1 when the row is the calling @deviceId.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.Device SET PasskeyCredentialId/PasskeyPublicKey/PasskeyCounter/PasskeyTransports = NULL, updatedAt = GETDATE() WHERE id = @targetDeviceId AND UserId = @userId AND removed = 0 AND PasskeyCredentialId IS NOT NULL (inside a transaction).
INSERT LOG.GeneralLog ('HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey', 'Passkey removed', userId, 'device=… label=… by=…') — audit trail of the revocation, in the same transaction.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 1950 (pre-flight, outside the transaction), 1951 (after ROLLBACK, so the row survives) and in the CATCH.

codeSmells.issue: Passkey columns are not in db/schema/tables/HC.Device.Table.sql
codeSmells.detail: PasskeyCredentialId NVARCHAR(500), PasskeyPublicKey NVARCHAR(2000), PasskeyCounter BIGINT and PasskeyTransports NVARCHAR(100) were added by db/hc6/public-web/archive/2026-09-16_device_passkey.sql and the schema file has not been refreshed. Nothing wrong in the SP; the schema snapshot is stale.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
